cards.front: Complete the guidance about instruction permits, beginning with “To obtain the instruction permit described for applicants under”.
cards.back: To obtain the instruction permit described for applicants under eighteen, the applicant must be at least fourteen and pass both the vision and knowledge tests.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about instruction permits, beginning with “The instruction permit for an applicant under eighteen expires”.
cards.back: The instruction permit for an applicant under eighteen expires after five years or when the valid United States-presence documents expire, whichever comes first.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about instruction permits, beginning with “An instruction-permit holder aged fourteen through seventeen ordinarily must”.
cards.back: An instruction-permit holder aged fourteen through seventeen ordinarily must keep the permit valid continuously for two hundred seventy-five days before upgrading to a restricted minor permit or operator license.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about instruction permits, beginning with “The minor’s instruction-permit holding period becomes one hundred eighty”.
cards.back: The minor’s instruction-permit holding period becomes one hundred eighty days after completing a Department of Education-approved driver-education course with at least eighty percent on both its written and driving portions.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about instruction permits, beginning with “A minor instruction-permit holder must drive with a parent”.
cards.back: A minor instruction-permit holder must drive with a parent or legal guardian, or another adult holding a valid license and at least one year of driving experience.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about instruction permits, beginning with “The adult supervising an instruction-permit holder must”.
cards.back: The adult supervising an instruction-permit holder must sit in the seat next to the driver.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about instruction permits, beginning with “A minor instruction-permit driver must complete fifty hours of”.
cards.back: A minor instruction-permit driver must complete fifty hours of adult-supervised driving, including ten hours in inclement weather and ten hours after dark.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about instruction permits, beginning with “For the instruction-permit route headed Over eighteen,”.
cards.back: For the instruction-permit route headed Over eighteen, applicants must pass the vision and knowledge tests.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about instruction permits, beginning with “The permit in the handbook’s Over eighteen route lasts”.
cards.back: The permit in the handbook’s Over eighteen route lasts five years or until the valid United States-presence documents expire, whichever is earlier.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about instruction permits, beginning with “A permit holder on the handbook’s Over eighteen route”.
cards.back: A permit holder on the handbook’s Over eighteen route must pass a drive test before upgrading to an operator license.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about instruction permits, beginning with “The adult supervising the handbook’s Over eighteen instruction-permit driver”.
cards.back: The adult supervising the handbook’s Over eighteen instruction-permit driver must have a valid driver license and at least one year of driving experience.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about instruction permits, beginning with “Instruction-permit holders cannot use a wireless communication device”.
cards.back: Instruction-permit holders cannot use a wireless communication device while driving a motor vehicle on public roads.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about instruction permits, beginning with “For permit restrictions, a wireless communication device means wireless”.
cards.back: For permit restrictions, a wireless communication device means wireless electronic equipment that provides voice or data communication between at least two parties.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about instruction permits, beginning with “The permit-related wireless-device definition includes cellular phones, texting devices,”.
cards.back: The permit-related wireless-device definition includes cellular phones, texting devices, message-capable personal digital assistants, message-capable audio-video players and laptop computers.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about restricted minor permits, beginning with “A restricted minor permit applicant must be at least”.
cards.back: A restricted minor permit applicant must be at least fourteen, complete the instruction-permit requirements, pass the drive test and have no traffic-violation conviction during the preceding six months.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about restricted minor permits, beginning with “The handbook allows an individual up to”.
cards.back: The handbook allows an individual up to age eighteen to hold a restricted minor permit.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about restricted minor permits, beginning with “A restricted minor permit lasts five years or until”.
cards.back: A restricted minor permit lasts five years or until the valid United States-presence documents expire, whichever happens first.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about restricted minor permits, beginning with “From six a.m. to ten p.m., a restricted minor”.
cards.back: From six a.m. to ten p.m., a restricted minor permit holder may drive with the parent’s or guardian’s permission while carrying the permit in immediate physical possession.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about restricted minor permits, beginning with “Between ten p.m. and six a.m., the ordinary restricted-minor”.
cards.back: Between ten p.m. and six a.m., the ordinary restricted-minor rule requires a parent or legal guardian seated next to the driver.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about restricted minor permits, beginning with “A restricted minor permit must be”.
cards.back: A restricted minor permit must be used for at least six months.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about restricted minor permits, beginning with “During the first six months on a restricted minor”.
cards.back: During the first six months on a restricted minor permit, passengers are limited to immediate family or household members.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about restricted minor permits, beginning with “A restricted minor permit converts automatically to”.
cards.back: A restricted minor permit converts automatically to an operator license when its holder reaches eighteen.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about restricted minor permits, beginning with “After ten p.m., a restricted minor permit holder may”.
cards.back: After ten p.m., a restricted minor permit holder may drive alone on the most direct route to or from school, a school event, church, a church event or work, and the handbook also lists unregistered agricultural machinery and farm-related work.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about restricted minor permits, beginning with “Restricted minor permit holders cannot use wireless communication”.
cards.back: Restricted minor permit holders cannot use wireless communication devices while operating a motor vehicle on public roads.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about operator-license requirements, beginning with “An operator-license applicant must be at least sixteen”.
cards.back: An operator-license applicant must be at least sixteen and have passed the vision, knowledge and driving tests.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about operator-license requirements, beginning with “An operator-license applicant aged sixteen or seventeen must satisfy”.
cards.back: An operator-license applicant aged sixteen or seventeen must satisfy the applicable instruction-permit or restricted-minor-permit requirements and have no traffic-violation conviction in the previous six months.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about operator-license requirements, beginning with “An operator license lasts five years or until”.
cards.back: An operator license lasts five years or until the valid United States-presence documents expire, whichever comes first.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about operator-license requirements, beginning with “The handbook’s printed prices list thirty-eight dollars each for”.
cards.back: The handbook’s printed prices list thirty-eight dollars each for the under-eighteen instruction permit, the Over eighteen instruction permit, the restricted minor permit and the operator license.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “License-test applicants must cooperate with the”.
cards.back: License-test applicants must cooperate with the examiner and follow the examiner’s instructions.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “An on-road test applicant must supply”.
cards.back: An on-road test applicant must supply a safe vehicle for the test.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “Pets and passengers are not permitted in”.
cards.back: Pets and passengers are not permitted in the vehicle during the on-road licensing test.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “The handbook recommends leaving children and pets away from”.
cards.back: The handbook recommends leaving children and pets away from the exam station and prohibits them in the testing area and during the drive test.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “A person may apply for a South Dakota”.
cards.back: A person may apply for a South Dakota operator license at any examination station in the state.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “Ordinary license renewal may occur up to one hundred”.
cards.back: Ordinary license renewal may occur up to one hundred eighty days before expiration, except when the applicant is turning twenty-one at renewal.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “A license expiring thirty days after its holder’s twenty-first”.
cards.back: A license expiring thirty days after its holder’s twenty-first birthday may be renewed on that birthday or during the next thirty days.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “An application for a South Dakota license requires surrender”.
cards.back: An application for a South Dakota license requires surrender of all South Dakota and out-of-state licenses and identification cards at application time.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “Transferring a currently valid out-of-state license ordinarily requires no”.
cards.back: Transferring a currently valid out-of-state license ordinarily requires no testing, but the handbook excludes a license with a hazardous-materials endorsement from that exemption.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “When an out-of-state license is transferred, the prior”.
cards.back: When an out-of-state license is transferred, the prior state is notified and its credentials become invalid.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “Examiners cannot issue a license to”.
cards.back: Examiners cannot issue a license to an applicant physically incapable of driving.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “An examiner may require testing”.
cards.back: An examiner may require testing when an applicant appears physically impaired.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “The licensing procedure includes taking the applicant’s”.
cards.back: The licensing procedure includes taking the applicant’s photograph each time the applicant comes in.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “If glasses or contacts are used for the”.
cards.back: If glasses or contacts are used for the vision test, they must also be worn when driving.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “After failing the vision test, an applicant must provide”.
cards.back: After failing the vision test, an applicant must provide an optometrist’s or ophthalmologist’s statement certifying safe-driving visual ability before proceeding with the examination.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “The required knowledge test covers”.
cards.back: The required knowledge test covers road rules and safe driving practices.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “A person caught cheating must wait at least two”.
cards.back: A person caught cheating must wait at least two weeks before retesting rather than retest the next day.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “The driving test uses normal driving tasks to let”.
cards.back: The driving test uses normal driving tasks to let the applicant demonstrate safe vehicle operation, without requiring illegal actions.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “At publication, the handbook required advance”.
cards.back: At publication, the handbook required advance scheduling for drive tests at every location.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “After failing any licensing test, an applicant cannot retest”.
cards.back: After failing any licensing test, an applicant cannot retest before the next working day and may choose to wait longer to study or practice.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about examination procedures, beginning with “Each paid test fee allows three testing opportunities within”.
cards.back: Each paid test fee allows three testing opportunities within six months, and three failures during that period require another fee.
